title: Translating Data into Feelings: Empathetic Character Gauges Transform Real-Time Electricity and Water Use into Emotions Designed to Motivate Conservation
finding: Studies examine how people interpret character gauges, respond emotionally to resource use and connect with nature.

authors: Jauernig, J.; et al. (incl. J. Petersen)

title: Overcoming Pluralistic Ignorance: Brief Exposure to Positive Thoughts and Actions of Others Can Enhance Social Norms Related to Climate Action and Support for Climate Policy
authors: Kearney, B.; Petersen, J.E.; Frantz, C.M.
finding: People underestimate how much others care. For 969 people, a short look at Community Voices made climate action feel normal.

authors: Jordan, R.; Gray, S.; Sorensen, A.; Frantz, C.M.; Brehm, P.; Shammin, M.; Petersen, J.E.; Boyse-Peacor, A.; Jauernig, J.

title: Changing culture through pro-environmental messaging delivered on digital signs: A longitudinal field study
finding: After two years of screens in six places, people of color reported stronger green norms, residents felt more connected to their town and its nature, and more said they save electricity.

title: Promoting systems thinking through perspective taking when using an online modeling tool
authors: Jordan, R.C.; Gray, S.; Boyse-Peacor, A.; Sorensen, A.E.; Frantz, C.M.; Jauernig, J.; Brehm, P.; Shammin, Md R.; Petersen, J.

title: Novel approach to delivering pro-environmental messages significantly shifts norms and motivation, but children are not more effective spokespeople than adults
authors: Frantz, C.M.; Petersen, J.E.; Lucaites, K.
finding: Community Voices raised concern, perceived norms and commitment to act. Children were no more persuasive than adults.

title: An animated visual representation of real-time resource flows through a community enhances systems thinking
authors: Petersen, J.E.; Frantz, C.M.; Tincknell, E.; Canning, C.
finding: Citywide Dashboard improved systems thinking for students initially less connected to nature. Brief exposure also widened adults' view of cause and effect.

title: Teaching systems thinking to 4th and 5th graders using Environmental Dashboard display technology
authors: Clark, S.; Petersen, J.E.; Frantz, C.M.; Roose, D.; Ginn, J.; Rosenberg-Daneri, D.
finding: Dashboard lessons improved content retention and systems thinking in six classes. Passive exposure alone had no measurable effect.

authors: Petersen, J.E.; Rosenberg-Daneri, D.; Frantz, C.; Shammin, Md R.
finding: Feedback at three scales: a building, a town's resource flows, and neighbors' words.

title: The role of students in the co-creation of transformational knowledge and sustainability experiments: Experiences from Sweden, Japan and the USA (chapter, Engaging Stakeholders in Education for Sustainable Development at University Level)
authors: Trencher, G.; Rosenberg-Daneri, D.; McCormick, K.; Terada, T.; Petersen, J.; Yarime, M.; Kiss, B.

title: Electricity and water conservation on college and university campuses in response to national competitions among dormitories: Quantifying relationships between behavior, conservation strategies and psychological metrics
authors: Petersen, J.E.; Frantz, C.M.; Shammin, Md R.; Yanisch, T.M.; Tincknell, E.; Myers, N.
finding: In 2010, dorms cut electricity 4% and water 6%; the top tenth cut 28% and 36%. Saving tracked dashboard visits.

title: Dormitory residents reduce electricity consumption when exposed to real-time visual feedback and incentives
authors: Petersen, J.E.; Shunturov, V.; Janda, K.; Platt, G.; Weinberger, K.
venue: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education 8:16-33
finding: Electricity fell 32%. Dorms with live feedback cut 55%, against 31% with weekly readings.
